entries.title: Translation obstructs a fixed-lattice defect penalty
entries.statement: On T_L=(R/LZ)^3, integer L>=2, X={0,...,L-1}^3 and Y=X+(1/2,0,0), every Y point has distance 1/2 from X, while E(Y)=E(X) for every translation-invariant E. Hence no c>0 uniformly lower-bounds E(Y)-E(X) by c times the number of points farther than delta from X when 0<delta<1/2. Scope: Does not establish or disprove a phase-fitted/boundary-pinned coercivity estimate or the full Riesz Gibbs target.
entries.proof_text: Simultaneously translate all coordinates by (1/2,0,0); energy is unchanged, each nearest-reference distance is exactly 1/2, and bad-site count is L^3.
assumptions: Defects counted against a fixed absolute reference X

entries.title: Draft: Mean-zero acoustic modes have no volume-uniform displacement gap
entries.statement: DRAFT concept; independent review pending. For L>=3, kappa>0 and periodic nearest-neighbor vector elasticity H=(kappa/2)sum_{x,j}|u(x+e_j)-u(x)|^2 on (Z/LZ)^3, the mean-zero field u(x)=a cos(2pi x_1/L)e_2 has H/sum_x|u(x)|^2=2kappa sin^2(pi/L). No positive constant c independent of L gives H>=c sum_x|u(x)|^2 on all mean-zero fields. Scope: Application to a Riesz Hessian requires a proved acoustic comparison; none is asserted here.

entries.title: Draft: Matching and displacement bounds imply finite-volume Fourier order
entries.statement: DRAFT concept; independent review pending. Let exactly N particles be measurably matched to N Bravais lattice sites with m unmatched particles/sites, matched positions p_j+a+u_j, and nonzero reciprocal vector G. Put A=N^{-1}sum_y exp(iG.y), b=1-2E(m/N)-(2N)^{-1}E sum_matched(G.u_j)^2. Configurationwise Re(exp(-iG.a)A)>=1-2m/N-(2N)^{-1}sum_matched(G.u_j)^2, and if b>=0 then E|A|^2>=b^2. Scope: Derive the mismatch and displacement estimates under the full Riesz Gibbs law, prove the appropriate infinite-volume equilibrium equations, and establish the full target periodicity.
assumptions: Equal fixed particle and reference-site counts N
Measurable possibly random global phase and matching
Finite expectation of matched squared projected displacements
G.p in 2pi Z on the reference Bravais lattice

entries.title: Draft: Soft short-range Gibbs laws allow vacancies in every bounded region
entries.statement: DRAFT concept; independent review pending. For an ordinary grand-canonical DLR Gibbs law in R^3 for V(x)=|x|^{-s}, s>3, at finite beta>0 and finite activity z>0, P(N_C=0|exterior)>=exp(-z|C|)>0 for every bounded finite-volume region C. Such a law cannot enforce at least one particle in a fixed bounded lattice tube almost surely. Scope: No identical bound is asserted for long-range neutralized jellium or canonical specifications. Defect control, rather than defect exclusion, is still needed.
assumptions: No external pinning or hard occupancy constraint
Conditional energies normalized relative to the empty interior

entries.title: Draft: Uniform displacement variance in cubic harmonic elasticity
entries.statement: DRAFT concept; independent review pending. For the zero-mean nearest-neighbor vector Gaussian elastic law on (Z/LZ)^3, L>=3, with H=(kappa/2)sum_{x,j}|u(x+e_j)-u(x)|^2 and beta,kappa>0, T_L=L^{-3}sum_{k!=0}[4sum_j sin^2(pi k_j/L)]^{-1}<=13/16. Consequently E exp(iG.u(x))=exp(-|G|^2 T_L/(2beta kappa))>=exp(-13|G|^2/(32beta kappa))>0. Scope: No derivation of the Riesz Hessian or unrestricted defect/anharmonic/DLR control is supplied.
assumptions: Exactly quadratic vector law on the mean-zero subspace

entries.title: Draft: An extensive energy gap alone does not suppress Gibbs defects
entries.statement: DRAFT concept; independent review pending. For beta,tau>0 and H_n=0 on [0,exp(-n^2)] and tau*n elsewhere in [0,1], the bad set has pointwise energy gap tau*n, yet its normalized Gibbs probability tends to 1 as n tends to infinity. Thus an extensive energy gap alone does not imply exponentially rare defects. Scope: This is not a Riesz example; establish the actual contour repair energy, multiplicity and Jacobian under the unrestricted gas.

entries.title: Draft: A continuum defect comparison needs energy and measure control
entries.statement: DRAFT concept; independent review pending. For a Lebesgue Gibbs law on Omega subset R^D and a contour event B, assume a piecewise C^1 map T:B->Omega satisfies the area formula, multiplicity<=M, |det DT|>=J>0 almost everywhere and H(x)-H(Tx)>=Delta. Then P(B)<=M exp(-beta Delta)/J. Scope: A full-dimensional moment-compatible repair with these bounds has not been constructed for the Riesz target.

entries.title: Draft: Exact rigid repairs collapse continuum configuration volume
entries.statement: DRAFT concept; independent review pending. For k>=2, a differentiable map on an open subset of R^{3k} whose output is a common translation of a fixed labeled k-point template has derivative rank at most 3 and determinant zero. A finite union of output templates over label permutations is Lebesgue null. Such exact rigid repair maps on a positive-volume domain cannot satisfy C7's area-formula and positive-Jacobian premises. Scope: Does not exclude repairs retaining full-dimensional displacement freedom or collective screening arguments.
assumptions: Open domain for the differential statement
Only a common translation is retained in the fixed-template output

entries.title: Draft: unrestricted crystalline reconstruction for neutral Riesz gas
entries.statement: UNPROVED INPUT for a chosen contour route. In dimension three fix 0<s<3, density rho>0, finite inverse temperature beta>0 and a neutral canonical Riesz jellium container with N=rho times its volume. To extend a phase-selected lattice calculation to the unrestricted gas, construct admissible same-N continuum defect repairs with volume-uniform positive energy gain per contour size and an exponential bound on the repaired reference-measure density. Include the actual exterior/background energy and dipole sector; retain full-dimensional configuration volume. Separately derive small phase-fitted mismatch/displacement moments, an unperturbed infinite-volume Gibbs limit, and a stated positional-order criterion. Compact dipole-free interaction estimates and harmonic variance bounds do not establish these inputs. No solution or novelty is claimed.
assumptions: Chosen long-range neutral canonical subtarget, not a fully quantified interpretation of every Riesz exponent
No proved reconstruction premise is supplied

relations.rationale: The chosen contour route requires a valid energy and reference-measure comparison; C7 gives one sufficient conditional form.
This route uses an explicit matching/displacement-to-Fourier implication after deriving its hypotheses; the Gibbs limit and full phase periodicity remain separate.
The exactly quadratic displacement bound illustrates the desired phonon control but proves none of the unrestricted Riesz defect hypotheses.
Both concern the same cubic harmonic operator: its smallest nonzero eigenvalue vanishes while its normalized inverse trace stays bounded.
The two-sector counterexample demonstrates why energy control alone cannot replace multiplicity/Jacobian or equivalent reference-measure control.
An exact rigid-template map has null image and cannot satisfy the comparison's positive Jacobian premise on a positive-volume domain.
A global phase must be accounted for before counting absolute lattice deviations; the Fourier reduction explicitly registers this phase.
